pr_title: Do not run TickerScheduleTriggerEngine watches if the schedule trigger engine is paused
pr_body:
This changes watcher to bail out of executing triggered watches if the watcher engine is paused. It fixes the problem described in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105933#issuecomment-2093624251
Closes #105933
pr_comments: Hi @masseyke, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Some notes on the things I've tried so far in this PR:

1. **Fail when a watch is added to TickerScheduleTriggerEngine when the engine is paused**: Several tests failed when I did this. I believe all the tests were single-node though. It looks like the problem is that on startup we pause/restart watcher, and we expect any watches added during that time to be executed.
2. **Ignore any watches added to TickerScheduleTriggerEngine when the engine is paused**: As expected (based on what I found above), some tests failed because watches never ran as expected. SmokeTestWatcherWithSecurityIT.testSearchTransformHasPermissions() is an example. Nothing ever appeared in watcher history.
3. **Fail when we are executing a watch in TickerScheduleTriggerEngine when the engine is paused**. This broke on a handful of existent tests, I think during the same startup time mentioned above. I have a stress test locally, and it breaks long after a node has come up (during execution when a watch shard is moved off the node).
4. **Bail out of executing watches in TickerScheduleTriggerEngine when the engine is paused**. This seems to be a solution. I haven't been able to cause any test failures with it yet, anyway (including my local stress test).
Hi @masseyke, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

> I don't think the changes here will cause issues, but also not sure if they will fix the race condition.

I am not 100% sure that this will fix the issues either. But without these changes I can repeatably cause the race condition, and with them I have not been able to.

>  Also, as-is there is only a very, very small window of difference between clearing the schedules.

I think that this is why it happens fairly rarely in the wild and is so hard to reproduce. But if it does happen, the impact is pretty bad -- the watch will continue to run forever.

issue_context.title: Watcher executes on a node after the .watches shard has been moved to a different node
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.8.2 (but likely others as well)

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

n/a

### Problem Description

This happens only rarely, but I have seen evidence of it twice in the same cluster a few days apart. As part of normal shard reallocation, a `.watches` shard gets moved off of a node (I'll call it `nodeA`) and onto another node (`nodeB`). This ought to mean that nodeA stops running watches. And we see in nodeA's logs:
```
paused watch execution, reason [no local watcher shards found], cancelled [0] queued tasks
```
But if we search `.watcher-history-*`, we see that now both nodeA and nodeB are executing the same watch, at nearly the same time on the same schedule. So instead of getting executed once every 10 minutes (for example), the watch gets executed twice every 10 minutes.
Aside from the message above, I haven't seen anything relevant in the logs. Restarting the nodes solves the problem.

### Steps to Reproduce

Unknown

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_
comments: Also, my initial thought was just that since watcher history records are written asynchronously, there could be a little lag. But it goes on for days until the cluster is restarted, with the same timestamps as the watcher history records from nodeB.

Here's how the race condition works:
Say I pause watcher because the shards have been allocated off of this machine. This happens more frequently due to the new shard allocator in 8.6.0. So [TickerScheduleTriggerEngine.pauseExecution()](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/watcher/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/watcher/trigger/schedule/engine/TickerScheduleTriggerEngine.java#L90) calls schedules.clear(). But while pause was running, there was a regularly-scheduled watch running. After pause completes, we get the result back, and thanks to WatcherIndexingListener, [we make sure to add the watch to the trigger service](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/watcher/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/watcher/WatcherIndexingListener.java#L142). TickerScheduleTriggerEngine.add sees that this watch is not in schedules so [it helpfully puts it in there for us](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/watcher/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/watcher/trigger/schedule/engine/TickerScheduleTriggerEngine.java#L103). So now this watch is running on this machine, and whatever machine the shard got allocated to!

I have tried to automate this race condition into a test, with no luck so far.

First I tried writing an AbstractWatcherIntegrationTestCase for it, before realizing that the class that I believe has the race condition (TickerScheduleTriggerEngine) is mocked out in that test with ScheduleTriggerEngineMock.

Then I tried writing an ESIntegTestCase briefly, before realizing that there was probably a reason so much was mocked in AbstractWatcherIntegrationTestCase -- I was unable to get the server to start up with Watcher running TickerScheduleTriggerEngine.

So I wrote an ESRestTestCase, based on SmokeTestWatcherTestSuiteIT. I brought up a 5-node cluster. I created a watch that executes every 10ms (which required a bit of a hack since we normally prevent that). I reallocate one of the two .watches shards constantly -- as soon as I find that it has finished reallocating, I move it again. I do this a few dozen times (all while the watch is running over and over). Then I look at the watch history, and wait until the most recent 10 entries have all run on the same node (if we hit the race condition I'd expect the watch to be running on 2 or more nodes). Unfortunately the test succeeds every single time. I also artificially slowed down the watch, hoping to make the race condition more likely. No luck.

review_comments: should this be moved a bit lower to the notify listeners and only notify them if it is running (else log the message) ? as-is there is not much difference between how race-like this can be. I think preventing the core action would help a bit more with the race like conditions.

There were a couple of reasons I did it here instead:
(1) I was trying to modify as little code as possible to avoid introducing some new bug or making things worse
(2) The real problem (in my opinion) isn't if a single event happens to slip through after the `.watches` shard has been moved -- it's that we just keep running events until the end of time. This bails out pretty quickly once the `.watches` shard has been moved.
